vignette_preview:
A male patient in his 20s presented with a 12-month history of asymptomatic red to brown macules and papules that initially appeared on his trunk and subsequently spread to the upper and proximal lower extremities. The lesions were symmetrically distributed and did not coalesce. His face, distal extremities, and mucous membranes were unaffected. The patient reported that some lesions had resolved spontaneously with residual hyperpigmentation. His medical history was unremarkable, and he did not take any medication on a regular basis.

- Multiple red to brown macules and papules on trunk and extremities- Symmetrically distributed lesions that did not coalesce- Face, distal extremities, and mucous membranes unaffected- No lymphadenopathy- Other systems review unremarkable

Laboratory Tests:- Blood cell count showed hypereosinophilia (4220/μL; reference range 50-250/μL)- Elevated tryptase (33.7 ng/mL; reference range <11.5 ng/mL)- Elevated vitamin B12 (>6000 pg/mL; reference range 211-911 pg/mL)- Negative serologic tests for HIV, hepatitis A, B, and C- Negative tests for parasitic infectionsImaging Studies:- CT of chest, abdomen, and pelvis: no pathologic findings- Cranial MRI: no pat
